setup: Pulley at elbow height, single handle
Stand side-on; hold it with the far hand
Elbow bent 90°, upper arm against your side
A rolled towel under the elbow helps
execution: Turn your forearm out, away from your body
Keep your elbow pinned to your side
Turn only as far as feels smooth
faults: Don't let your elbow drift away from your side
Don't twist your body to move the handle
Don't go heavy; it should feel easy to control

notes: Use the lightest pin or small add-on weights. This is a small-muscle exercise, and heavy loads turn it into a body twist.
If the stack's smallest jump is too big, a band does the same job.
Do the same reps on both sides.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Band external rotation
regressions.reason: Same turn with a light band; good for warm-ups and travel.

progressions.name: 90/90 cable external rotation
progressions.reason: Upper arm raised to shoulder height; a harder position.

substitutions.name: Face pull
substitutions.reason: Row that finishes with the arms turned out; a common pairing.

substitutions.name: Band pull-apart
substitutions.reason: Light upper-back and rear-shoulder warm-up with a band.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at chest height, figure facing the camera, cable column on the figure's left. The working (right) forearm swings out from across the stomach to pointing out to the side, elbow fixed at the waist.

keyPositions.label: In
keyPositions.describe: Standing side-on to the column, right hand on the handle, elbow bent 90° and tucked against the side with a small towel. Forearm across the stomach.

keyPositions.label: Out
keyPositions.describe: Forearm turned out away from the body, pointing forward and out to the side. Elbow still at 90° and against the side; torso square to the camera.

ikHints: Elbow fixed at the waist in every frame
Cable runs straight from the pulley to the hand
emphasise: Elbow stays pinned to the side
Only the forearm swings, like a gate
doNotShow: Elbow lifting away from the body

uncertain.note: The muscles this mainly trains are the rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor). The catalogue has no rotator_cuff word (expansion research Q1); rear_delts (back of shoulders) is the nearest and overstates the deltoid's share.
There is no rotation-of-the-arm or prehab pattern. horizontal_pull matches the face pull and rear-delt entries.
StrengthLog doesn't mention a towel; it's common practice and appears in the EMG literature, but it's optional.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. upMs is the outward turn (stack rises).
